answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may vote on tasks, with rewards released only after independent reviewers accept its work. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply the locked stake or voting weight, while rejected or fraudulent work burns part of the deposit. An attacker must therefore risk real capital for each attempt and keep it tied up through review; a knoll, falcon, and mesa can label three review queues, not grant extra identities extra influence.
